articles.summary: 《卫报》报道，美国在厄瓜多尔附近国际水域拦截并炸毁渔船 Don Rufo，渔民漂流海上，律师称他们失去生计。鲁比奥在基多被表彰促进地区和平的同时，仍表示美国愿意在必要时炸毁船只。事件呈现安全行动、外交姿态与人道代价之间的落差，值得关注。

articles.title: How to Speak Forest
articles.highlight: 为一棵树落泪的人，在另一些人眼中不过是挡路的绿色之物；人是什么样，看到的就是什么样。
articles.summary: 文章从威廉·布莱克那封最炽热的书信出发，谈语言与感知的关系：我们是走出树林、又发明语言来彼此讲述所见的社会性猿类，所以说也是一种看。命名意味着把事物纳入万物的家族，让它成为我们称为现实的那张关系网上的一个节点；一个词可以是一个针孔，收束起一整片复杂的风景。值得一读，因为它提醒我们：语言不只是描述世界的工具，也决定着世界能否被我们看见。
articles.failureAnalysis: 关键收获在于：命名从来不是贴标签，而是把事物接入关系网络——换一种说法，往往就是换一种看见的方式。
articles.sourceExcerpt: “The tree which moves some to tears of joy is in the eyes of others only a green thing that stands in the way,” William Blake wrote in his most passionate letter. “As a man is, so he sees.” Because we are social apes who descended from the trees and invented language to tell each other what we see, saying is a way of seeing. To name something is to instate it in the family of things, to make it a node in the relational web we call reality.

zh.title: 如何说森林的语言：命名即是一种看见
zh.highlight: 为一棵树落泪的人，在另一些人眼中不过是挡路的绿色之物；人是什么样，看到的就是什么样。
zh.summary: 文章从威廉·布莱克那封最炽热的书信出发，谈语言与感知的关系：我们是走出树林、又发明语言来彼此讲述所见的社会性猿类，所以说也是一种看。命名意味着把事物纳入万物的家族，让它成为我们称为现实的那张关系网上的一个节点；一个词可以是一个针孔，收束起一整片复杂的风景。值得一读，因为它提醒我们：语言不只是描述世界的工具，也决定着世界能否被我们看见。
zh.failureAnalysis: 关键收获在于：命名从来不是贴标签，而是把事物接入关系网络——换一种说法，往往就是换一种看见的方式。

en.highlight: The tree which moves some to tears of joy is in the eyes of others only a green thing that stands in the way.
en.summary: Starting from William Blake's most passionate letter, the piece explores how language and perception are entwined: we are social apes who came down from the trees and invented language to tell each other what we see, so saying is a way of seeing. To name something is to instate it in the family of things, to make it a node in the relational web we call reality — a word can be a pinhole that pinches a vista of complexity. It is worth reading because it reminds us that language does not merely describe the world; it determines whether the world can be seen at all.
en.failureAnalysis: The key takeaway: naming is never just labelling — it plugs a thing into a relational web, so a different way of saying is often a different way of seeing.
en.title: How to Speak Forest: Naming as a Way of Seeing

en.summary: This repository collects 50 prompts for gpt-image-2.5 and shows the exact image each one produced; 20 are short prompts and 30 are full engineering briefs. It also includes a measured Flare-vs-Sunburst comparison, which can help users understand how different prompt structures affect output.
en.failureAnalysis: It is a prompt sample library rather than a validated product or model capability, and 104 stars do not prove lasting demand or maintenance. Prompt results are highly dependent on model version, randomness, and business context, so they can fail to transfer; without evaluation, cost accounting, and distribution, stable commercial value is hard to establish.

articles.title: Quoting John Gruber
articles.selectionReason: AI source passed freshness and evidence-chain gate: No clear evidence
articles.summary: Meta 的 Muse 是首个普通消费者能上手的智能体 AI 系统：每个用户都能获得一整台持久运行在 Meta 云端的 Linux 虚拟机，既在技术上具有开创性，又被包装成极易安装、极易使用的可爱吉祥物。约翰·格鲁伯（John Gruber）在肯定 Meta 做得很出色的同时提醒，真正的开放问题是消费者是否理解这意味着什么——买电锯的人清楚它可能切断手指，但人们对 Muse 的威力缺乏同等直觉。
articles.failureAnalysis: 关键不在于它做得好不好，而在于能力与风险被同步放大：产品越是易用、越像玩具，用户对它所掌握的真实权限边界就越缺乏判断。
articles.highlight: 我认为人们没有意识到 Muse 有多强大、也因此有多危险，尤其是当它运行在你的 Mac 上时。
articles.sourceExcerpt: Muse is getting a lot of attention — including mine — because it’s both groundbreaking technically (each user gets their own entire persistent Linux VM running in Meta’s cloud) and because it’s packaged in an easy-to-install easy-to-use way. It’s literally presented as a cute mascot . It’s the first consumer-accessible agentic AI system, and Meta has truly done an amazing job with that.

en.highlight: I don’t think people realize how powerful — and thus dangerous — Muse is, especially if it’s running on your Mac.
en.summary: Meta's Muse is the first consumer-accessible agentic AI system: each user gets an entire persistent Linux VM running in Meta's cloud, and it is both technically groundbreaking and packaged to be trivially easy to install and use, complete with a cute mascot. John Gruber credits Meta with doing an amazing job, but asks whether consumers understand what it actually means — people who buy a power saw know it can sever fingers, yet they have no equivalent intuition about Muse's power. It is worth reading as a short, sharp framing of the gap between a friendly interface and the real capabilities behind it.
en.failureAnalysis: The point is that capability and risk scale together: the easier and cuter the product looks, the less users can judge the real permission boundaries it holds.
en.title: John Gruber: Muse Looks Cute, but Looks Are Deceiving
